title: Real Estate Makes No Financial Sense. I Still Want a Home.
meta_title: Should You Buy a Flat in India? The Honest Math
subtitle: A ₹1.5 crore flat is a genuinely bad investment once you count the hidden costs. But a home is not an investment, and renting at 60 is its own kind of risk. So do you buy now, or buy later?
description: The honest math on buying a flat in India: rental yield, GST, stamp duty, furnishing, repairs, vacancy, and the opportunity cost that make a ₹1.5 crore flat a poor investment, why renting usually wins on the spreadsheet, and whether to buy your home now or near retirement.
toast: Real estate is a terrible investment and a wonderful home. The trick is knowing which one you are actually buying.
You pay a 9% home loan to own an asset that yields 3%. That gap is the price of feeling settled.

faqs.question: Is buying a flat a good investment in India?
faqs.answer: Usually not, once you count stamp duty, GST, furnishing, maintenance, property tax, and vacant months against a rental yield of only around 3%. Over the long run, money left in equity has tended to grow far faster than a built flat appreciates, so as a pure investment a flat usually loses to renting and investing the difference. As a home you actually live in, the calculation is a different one.

faqs.question: Should I buy or rent a house in India?
faqs.answer: On the spreadsheet, renting and investing the difference usually wins, because you pay a home loan rate of around 8.75% to own an asset that yields only about 3% in rent. Renting makes the most sense while you are mobile and might move for work or family. Buying starts to make sense when you know you will stay put for 10 years or more and you value the security of your own place over the returns you give up.

faqs.question: How much does buying a ₹1.5 crore flat in India actually cost?
faqs.answer: Well over ₹1.5 crore. A new flat adds roughly 7% stamp duty plus registration and 5% GST, which is around ₹18 lakh in taxes alone, and then furnishing can add another ₹8 to ₹12 lakh. After that come society maintenance, property tax, repairs, and the months the flat sits empty between tenants. A resale flat skips the GST but carries everything else.

faqs.question: Is it better to buy a home now or near retirement?
faqs.answer: Mathematically, renting and investing the difference usually leaves you able to buy a home later from a much bigger corpus, because equity has tended to outgrow real estate over long periods. That assumes you actually invest the difference and do not need the stability of your own home while raising a family. Buying earlier mostly buys you security and control rather than investment returns.
